articles.title_orig: A Sam Altman parody offers an amusing lesson in memory management
articles.title_zh: A Sam Altman parody offers an amusing lesson in memory management
articles.content_orig:
Sam Altman’s recent comments on the Cheeky Pint podcast inspired developer Iain Kay to create a satirical script that allows users to email the OpenAI CEO once per day if more than 10 percent of their system RAM is reported as available. Ram-Altman is described by its creator as a “parody project” launched in response to Altman’s viral remarks about RAM in your personal PC.
As reported by The Verge , on the October 29 episode recorded with Stripe President John Collison, Altman said, “A lot of people want local inference. And somehow, they assume that the problem is solved now because we are going to have open source models, we’re going to be able to run them on our computers, and so we’re not going to need all the stuff in the data center. But from a global allocation perspective, actually, it’s quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world’s limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer and being used 5 percent of the time.”
Altman has since explained that his comments were taken out of context and briefly changed his display name to “RAM Altman” on X, which Kay calls on the project GitHub, “objectively excellent and where the project gets its name.”
In an email to Ars, Kay said, “Ram-Altman is a bash script that takes MemTotal minus MemAvailable from /proc/meminfo, so the figure includes page cache and reclaimable slab but leaves out tmpfs and shared memory.”
If the script only showed what Linux reports as “free” RAM, it would paint an incomplete picture. Linux often reports a surprisingly small amount of “free” RAM, as it doesn’t count memory that is currently claimable for use. Linux will fill available RAM caches with file data for quick access, but the kernel can reclaim that usage at a moment’s notice when needed. The MemAvailable figure is the kernel’s own estimate of how much memory it could hand over without swapping.
Users can schedule the script to ask the kernel for a status update every five minutes, and if more than 10 percent of RAM is available, it triggers a joke email from one of several joke templates. The script limits outgoing emails to one per day.
The GitHub page for the RAM-Altman project includes a dry-run option that any Linux user with a Bash terminal should be able to paste and run without the need for email trolling. When the threshold is exceeded, each dry run output features one generated joke email, so repeated runs produce different amusing examples.
A test run of the script on my Fedora 44 KDE machine confirmed the author’s measurements. Inside the System – Info Center of my Fedora desktop, the system reports 14.9 GiB of total usable system RAM after the kernel and firmware take their needed slices of the 16 GiB of physical memory. This reflects the total amount of capacity the system has to work with, not the amount available at any given time. The Ram-Altman script shows that of that 14.9 GiB total pool, 10 GiB is used, with 4.9 GiB available (33.1 percent). That figure isn’t the simple sum of the “free” and “cache” lines that the script displays, but a kernel-calculated figure that accounts for the full amount of memory that can be reclaimed.
The project concedes the nuance that Altman was referring to how much time memory spends being utilized, while the script measures how much capacity is free at the time of measurement. While the script might tell Altman that 33 percent of your system RAM is available, it doesn’t outline how often that’s the case. The concession steps on the joke slightly, but it keeps everyone honest.
The GitHub is wise to point out that “ --dry-run is the best way to enjoy this. It costs nothing and all the jokes are there.” Used irresponsibly, this cheeky joke could morph into a harassment tool, and Kay quickly points out that the script does not include anyone’s email, including Altman’s. Users who deploy their own operating version are encouraged to only use their own real email addresses and honor any requests to stop, as is outlined at the bottom of the script-generated output.
If you’re interested in taking a look at some of the emails generated without having to spin up a Linux machine that reports the system status every five minutes, the ram-altman.lol project website rotates through sample emails generated by the script. Kay writes on the website that, “In fairness, he says the remarks were taken out of context , posted ‘i want you to have so much ram’ , and briefly went by Ram Altman on X. That makes this script a daily progress report.”

articles.title_orig: Who is Alice Huang, the woman linked to Nvidia’s CEO?
articles.title_zh: Who is Alice Huang, the woman linked to Nvidia’s CEO?
articles.content_orig:
CEO reportedly ‌had close relationship ‌with a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to ‌Beijing
Nvidia said ⁠on Sunday it “is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort”.
The New York Times reported in ​October that Donald Trump had been briefed last year on intelligence that Huang ‌had a close relationship ‌with a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to ‌Beijing.
Speaking to reporters on Sunday, Trump downplayed the revelations about Huang, who is an influential adviser to the president on artificial intelligence, saying: “I think he’s an honorable guy. I think he probably has an excuse for it.”
Trump also brushed off a question about whether he now regrets not acting on the intelligence when he was briefed on it, and suggested that he would be happy to take Huang with him on a trip to Asia next week. “I haven’t heard he’s done anything wrong,” Trump said. “He dealt with somebody. But, you know, so does everybody else.”
Republican lawmakers have expressed more alarm, asking Huang to give the House foreign affairs and intelligence committees a closed-door briefing next week on Nvidia’s “security protocols against foreign adversary espionage” and his relationship with Alice Huang or Huang Le, an executive at a Singapore-based datacenter company called Megaspeed, who is of no relation to the Nvidia CEO. She had previously been suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips to China, prompting American officials to surveil and monitor her.
Those officials have determined that she was acting as a Chinese intelligence asset, passing commercial information to Beijing, the New York Times reported, citing unnamed sources.
The company’s board said in a statement on Sunday that, while it has no reason to believe that either US national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, its inquiry will examine all available information.
“The Board prioritizes US national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders,” the company said. “The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate.”
Huang fully ‌supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it, it added.
Axios reported on ​Sunday, citing a draft email by Huang to employees, that Huang admitted to having a romantic relationship with a suspected Chinese spy and took full ⁠responsibility for his actions.
“I was unfaithful to my ​wife. My ​actions hurt her ​and our children. There is no excuse ​for what ‌I did,” ​Huang said ​in the draft email also seen by Reuters.
Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the Axios report.
The Times reported on Sunday that a memo drafted by US secretary of state Marco Rubio circulated among top policymakers in the Trump administration last spring, citing intelligence that the businesswoman who had a relationship with Nvidia’s chief executive was a spy for China’s ministry of state security. Despite those concerns, Huang was invited to join Trump’s delegation when he traveled to China in May. Huang and his wife, Lori Huang, were also invited to a state dinner at the White House in September for Xi Jinping and seated at the top table with Trump and China’s president.
Nvidia’s powerful chips serve as a cornerstone of the AI boom, placing Jensen Huang into one of the most influential leadership positions in the industry. In that position, he has developed a close partnership with Trump as the US government attempts to defend its position as a leader in AI development.
However, national security concerns have prompted strict US export controls, effectively barring the company from selling its top-tier processors to customers in China.
US officials have cited threats to the US supply chain and fears over national security risks as a rationale for the restrictions. Scott Bessent, the US treasury secretary, has also suggested that China could be sanctioned for theft of US data and intellectual property.
The Trump administration has imposed restrictions on exports of advanced AI chips to China as a matter of national security. Megaspeed’s Alice Huang was suspected to have been helping the government get around those restrictions.
The investigation also follows a rough few days on Wall Street for AI tech firms, particularly Nvidia. A sell-off of tech stocks that began earlier this month and gained steam with disappointing earnings led to a total decline of nearly $1tn in value off the tech-heavy Nasdaq exchange in one week and erased about $2tn in a month.
A drop of 3.1% for Nvidia, previously worth about $5tn, whose chips have made it the poster child of the AI frenzy, was the heaviest force pulling the S&P 500 downward recently.
Nick Robins-Early and Blake Montgomery contributed reporting

articles.title_zh: China extends pause on rare earth export curbs for two months
articles.content_orig:
China on Monday announced it is suspending export controls on some critical minerals for two months, preserving a broader trade deal struck between Washington and Beijing before an expected meeting between presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in Asia next week.
The announcement from China's Ministry of Commerce formalises an agreement to extend a bilateral trade truce that was set to expire on Tuesday. The extension runs to January 10, according to the ministry. China's finance ministry also said a 24 per cent tariff on US goods would be suspended for two months, although it will still charge a 10 per cent fee, according to a statement.
A filing from the Office of the US Trade Representative posted in the Federal Register also said it was suspending action from a Section 301 investigation into China 's maritime and logistic sectors. The US is also extending 178 current Section 301 tariff exclusions for Chinese goods, according to a second filing.
Where does Trump's critical minerals strategy go from here?
China announced a package of export controls on seven heavy rare earth elements last April, before expanding that list in October. It had earlier announced export curbs on battery supply chain chokepoints, including cathode materials, cathode precursors and graphite anode materials, widening a trade rift with Washington and stoking fears of a potential global supply chain crisis .
China accounted for 60 per cent of global mined production of magnet rare earths in 2024 and 91 per cent of global refined output, according to the International Energy Agency. It holds an even higher share for permanent magnet production.
The US and China entered into a one-year trade truce last October during their summit in Busan, South Korea, that paused tit-for-tat tariff measures, deferred rare earth curbs and included a pledge from China to resume importing US soybeans.
However, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent last week urged Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng to “fully and immediately” implement its commitments in Busan, while also raising concerns about “recent Chinese actions”, his department said in a statement.
In a separate statement, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said it remained important for China to fully implement its commitments, particularly in relation to agricultural purchases, rare earths and other critical minerals.
“There is an effort that has been co-ordinated between Treasury and the White House to track various commitments made by China since they first met in Busan,” said a former senior US official. “It's not just critical minerals; it is purchases of various agricultural products, where they stand on GE engines and Boeing,”
“And I think there are people … inside the US government that believe that China has overpromised and underdelivered, and they are making a consistent case that the issue that Bessent and Greer went out on was on critical minerals.”
Meanwhile, China said it “expressed serious concern” over recent US restrictions after Washington placed sanctions on two Chinese companies over their alleged ties to the Cuban regime's oil shipping networks supporting the Cuban military.
Mr Trump and Mr Xi are expected to hold a meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit held in Shenzhen next week. It would be the leaders' third meeting this year.

articles.title_orig: Warren Buffett's Rule for Stock Buybacks Is Very Specific. Berkshire Spent a Record $9.6 Billion on Them Last Quarter.
articles.title_zh: Warren Buffett's Rule for Stock Buybacks Is Very Specific. Berkshire Spent a Record $9.6 Billion on Them Last Quarter.
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE:BRKA)(NYSE:BRKB) has never spent this much on its own stock in one quarter. The company spent about $9.6 billion on repurchases in the third quarter of 2026. This inches past the nearly $9.3 billion it spent in the third quarter of 2020.
At Berkshire, a buyback also says something about price. The company repurchases shares only if management thinks they cost less than the business is worth.
Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »
And the Class B shares now trade near $570 as I write, about 12% over the average price Berkshire paid in September. I think the record buyback says a lot about what the stock was worth then, and a lot less about what it's worth at today's price.
Warren Buffett. Image source: Getty Images.
Warren Buffett , now Berkshire's chairman emeritus, spelled out his rule for repurchases in his 2011 letter to shareholders.
"Charlie and I favor repurchases when two conditions are met: first, a company has ample funds to take care of the operational and liquidity needs of its business; second, its stock is selling at a material discount to the company's intrinsic business value, conservatively calculated," he wrote, referring to his late partner, Charlie Munger.
Intrinsic value is an estimate of what a whole business is worth.
Versions of both tests remain in Berkshire's latest quarterly filing, which says it can repurchase shares whenever its CEO, after consulting the chairman of the board, "believes that the repurchase price is below Berkshire's intrinsic value, conservatively determined." These two roles now belong to Greg Abel and Howard Buffett, Warren's son.
Berkshire also won't buy back stock if doing so would push its cash and Treasury bills below $30 billion. And it had around $352 billion in both insurance and other businesses at the end of September, so the first test isn't a big hurdle.
The program no longer has a set price limit, though. Until 2018, Berkshire wouldn't pay over a 20% premium to book value (what's left after subtracting a company's liabilities from its assets). Based on a book value of about $358 per Class B share at the end of September, that limit would be roughly $429, well under the stock's 52-week low of about $464. So, Berkshire is buying at prices the old valuation limit wouldn't have allowed.
Showing how fast the buying has accelerated, Berkshire repurchased no stock in 2025. Then it bought around $235 million in the first quarter of 2026 and about $4.5 billion in the second quarter.
Across both share classes, Berkshire spent around $3.4 billion in July at an average of about $496 per Class B share, about $847 million in August at about $504, and about $5.4 billion in September at around $507. So its biggest month of buying came at its highest average price of the quarter.
The buying also seems to have kept going. Berkshire's share count dropped by the equivalent of about 3.8 million Class B shares from Sept. 30 to Oct. 28, suggesting about $2 billion more in buybacks. The filing doesn't give prices for those weeks, when the Class B shares closed between about $501 and $549.
A buyback signals to investors that the CEO believed the shares were worth more than the price paid. It doesn't say how much more. Sure, "conservatively determined" suggests the full value might be well above what Berkshire paid. But the company doesn't publish its estimate.
Today's buyer pays around 15% more than Berkshire's July average. That's a valuation of about 1.6 times book value at the end of September, up from around 1.4 times book value at September's average price.
The third quarter's numbers don't explain the stock's run-up since September, either. Berkshire's third-quarter operating earnings (which leave out the swings in its stock portfolio that skew net income) dropped around 6% year over year to about $12.7 billion. Without foreign-currency effects on Berkshire's debt, they dropped less than 1%. But insurance underwriting earnings fell about 43%.
At roughly $570, the stock trades at about 26 times last 12 months' operating earnings.
In the end, I think the record buyback is a strong sign that about $507 was a good price for Berkshire stock, and a far weaker one than about $570 is.
I'd still consider buying near $570, given how much cash Berkshire has left to deploy. But I'd be a lot more interested at prices closer to what Berkshire itself paid.

articles.title_orig: Pope Leo delivers veiled rebuke of austerity measures in predecessor’s homeland
articles.title_zh: Pope Leo delivers veiled rebuke of austerity measures in predecessor’s homeland
articles.content_orig:
Pope Leo XIV called on Argentine President Javier Milei and the country’s political leaders to “safeguard democracy” and demonstrate a “careful use of words” during his first speech in Buenos Aires.
The American pope arrived in Argentina on Sunday, embarking on a trip that his predecessor, the first Argentine pope, was never able to make.
Leo’s highly anticipated papal visit to Argentina began with a private meeting with President Milei shortly after the pope landed. Milei has received strong backing from US President Donald Trump, with whom Leo, first American pontiff, has publicly disagreed, particularly on the treatment of migrants and the war in Iran.
The pope’s visit comes at a time when Milei’s “chainsaw” austerity measures have led to welfare spending cuts. Milei has also equated state-led social justice programs with communism and has also been accused of undermining democracy through attacks on the press and divisive rhetoric. He has also struggled to secure bipartisan agreements.
“Democracy, then, is also a part of Argentina’s heritage that needs to be safeguarded,” the pope said at a meeting with politicians, members of civic society and the diplomatic corps at the Palacio Libertad. “Democracy is also strengthened by the daily conduct of public life: through willingness to listen, through careful use of words, through the patient search for agreement, and through the ability to see those who think differently as fellow citizens with whom we share a common future.”
The Chicago-born pontiff, who recently cast a mail-in ballot during the US mid-term elections, talked about the importance of the “freedom to elect one’s own leaders through the ballot box.” He urged leaders to recognize the limits of their power, and said that democracy is protected by “confidence in the law”, the ability to freely express convictions and for institutions to serve all parties.
“Authority is most authentic when it is exercised as service, when it looks beyond the immediate, and when it uses its power to promote the welfare of all,” the pope said. An eruption of applause from the audience forced him to repeat his next line: “Those who exercise authority have a duty to act with prudence, to acknowledge the limits of the power entrusted to them.”
Leo’s November 8-11 trip is the first papal visit to Argentina in almost four decades and it comes with the added dimension that Pope Francis did not make a return trip home during his 12-year-papacy. Millions are expected to attend the various services and events while the pope is in the country.
A mass held Monday drew a crowd of roughly 2.5 million people, according to official estimates, making it the largest event Pope Leo has held in his papacy thus far. It also surpasses the numbers that turned out in the same spot for Pope John Paul II in 1982.
One Argentine woman, Milagros, told CNN that Francis had baptized her before he became pope. She said Leo’s papacy had brought her back into the fold, and she now attends more religious services.
“The pope’s message reached me late, but it reached me,” Milagros said.
After mass, Leo visited with five people who had suffered abuse by Catholic clergy or within church organizations. A Vatican press release said the pope “greeted them together, imparted his blessing upon them, and expressed his gratitude for the meeting and for their witness of faith.”
Francis’ decision not to visit Argentina was something even his closest friends were unable to explain. Some have suggested the late pope’s reluctance to visit was linked to Argentina’s polarized political culture, with Francis wary that his presence in the country could be weaponized.
The Argentine pope had a strong emphasis on the church helping the most marginalized in society. Francis lamented Argentina’s economic decline which he blamed on decades of bad governance. He contrasted the roughly 5% inflation rate he recalled from his youth with the soaring inflation and high poverty rates of recent years.
In his speech, Leo cited Argentina’s “abundance of human resources” but called for its “wealth bear fruit for the benefit of all and warned that corruption undermines trust in institutions.
Before his election as pope in 2013, Francis served as archbishop of Buenos Aires, where he spoke out on social justice and was unafraid to criticize political leaders.
Leo’s visit, the second leg of his 12-day tour of South America, will underline the ways he continues the reforms of his predecessor, but with his own distinctive style.
Pope Leo, in contrast, has made the church’s social teaching and concern for the marginalized a central concern of his papacy. His itinerary in Argentina includes a visit to a federal prison in Buenos Aires and a stop at a care center for people with intellectual and physical disabilities in Claypole which has been affected by the Milei cuts.
During his presidential campaign and in the years leading up to it, Milei repeatedly insulted Francis, calling him an “imbecile” for defending social justice, “the representative of the evil one on earth” and a “sh*t of a pope.” Milei later apologized for these remarks and called Francis “the most important Argentine in history” following the pontiff’s death in April 2025, repeating the compliment in his remarks on Sunday.
Milei and Francis met in the Vatican in February 2024, with the pope joking with the president: “you cut your hair!” — a reference to the unruly hairstyle which earned Milei the nickname “The Wig.” Milei replied that he had “tidied it up.”
Leo and Milei previously met at the Vatican in June 2025. After meeting Milei in the Casa Rosada on his arrival in Buenos Aires, the pope was presented with the keys to the city of the Argentine capital by the mayor, Jorge Macri.
CNN’s Claudia Rebaza contributed to this report.

It's been a rough few weeks to own CoreWeave (NASDAQ:CRWV) or Nebius Group (NASDAQ:NBIS). Both stocks have lost close to half their value since early October. Both companies report earnings this week -- CoreWeave on Tuesday, followed by Nebius on Thursday -- that may have serious consequences for shareholders.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »
While the stocks have been sliding for some time, last Tuesday's sweeping Democratic midterm victory led to a roughly 14% drop in less than a week as investors weighed what the results would mean for the AI build-out.
Democratic candidates across the country ran on platforms that promised to rein in data center building and increase oversight of the AI industry at large. It worked. The topic became a flashpoint and helped propel Democrats to victory in states where the build-out is in full swing.
Data center moratoriums were central campaign pitches for the governors-elect in Texas, Ohio, and Georgia -- key states in the AI buildout.
CoreWeave has six active sites in Texas. Nebius faces its own challenges in states like Pennsylvania, which has already tightened its permitting rules and has a full moratorium under consideration.
The election results were hardly the start of the companies' recent woes. They've just amplified concerns over the sustainability of their business models -- especially given CoreWeave's heavy reliance on debt financing.
This is an expensive business. Without the resources of the big tech hyperscalers like Meta (NASDAQ:META) or Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN), CoreWeave has been forced to take on serious debt to fund its growth. The company currently carries $35.1 billion in on-the-books debt.
Concerns around the company's borrowing led the yield on some of CoreWeave's bonds above 16% as of last week. At the same time, the cost to insure those bonds against default skyrocketed.
Nebius, on the other hand, relies less on financing, carrying $8.5 billion. However, that could change. The company lined up a $3.5 billion loan facility from Citi in October, and Reuters reported that it was considering a high-yield bond sale, but ultimately passed.
And that was before the added risk of a data center construction slowdown.
Wall Street is expecting another big quarter from both companies. Analysts are looking for:
CoreWeave: $3.55 billion in sales, or about 160% growth
Nebius: $908 million, or about 500% growth
These are obviously extreme growth rates that any company would envy. I think both companies will have to overperform these targets while also showing costs are improving as a bare minimum.

If any delays are expected, how will that impact cash flows? What is CoreWeave's plan if borrowing costs keep rising? Can it afford to borrow at 16% interest, and for how long?
And for Nebius, does its recent $3.5 billion credit facility signal it will need to rely more on borrowing than it has in the past? How will this impact its cash flows?

articles.title_orig: Minnesota candy store owner charged over liquor-filled candy
articles.title_zh: Minnesota candy store owner charged over liquor-filled candy
articles.content_orig:
The owner of Minnesota's Largest Candy Store in Jordan is facing a gross misdemeanor count of selling an alcoholic product without a license after an anonymous tipster alleged a child was sold liquor-filled candies this summer without an ID check.
According to court documents filed last month in Scott County, the tip was sent to the Minnesota Department of Public Safety's Alcohol and Gambling Enforcement Division on July 1.
Later that month, agents with the department visited the store and found "a section dedicated to alcoholic beverage candies and confections," including Asbach Pralinen Brandy Cherries, according to the criminal complaint, with a alcohol concentration 7.3%, and a Goldkenn Jack Daniel's Tennessee Fire Swiss chocolate liqueur, with a 3.58% concentration.
The complaint states the agents observed warnings on the back of the products that state they can't be sold to minors, but "the items did not have a separate procedure compared to non-alcohol filled items."
Investigators allege when agents confronted the store's owner, 66-year-old Robert Mark Wagner, he confirmed he didn't have a liquor license, according to court documents, and was under the impression he "could sell all the alcoholic confections and beverage candies" he had in stock.
Wagner, of Belle Plaine, Minnesota, was not arrested. He's set to make his first court appearance on Dec. 18.
The charge against Wagner carries a maximum of a year in jail and a $3,000 fine, according to the county attorney's office.

articles.title_orig: China’s rare-earth rubber trades at 22,500 yuan a tonne, about 35% above standard rubber
articles.title_zh: China’s rare-earth rubber trades at 22,500 yuan a tonne, about 35% above standard rubber
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
China is testing whether a premium rubber can win a place in electric-vehicle tires. Rare-earth cis-butadiene rubber, made with a rare-earth catalyst, now has a Xinjiang plant rated at 100,000 metric tons a year, about 110,000 U.S. tons. It also trades at a higher price than conventional synthetic rubber.
China Rubber Industry Association data published Nov. 2 quoted rare-earth grade ND9106 at 22,500 yuan (about US$3,400) per metric ton during Oct. 26 to Nov. 1. Conventional BR9000 in Shandong province was quoted at 16,660 yuan per metric ton, so the rare-earth grade carried a premium of about 35%.
For tire makers, the rubber offers better wear resistance, greater strength and lower rolling resistance, and wider domestic production could make it more widely available.
A production unit at Dushanzi Petrochemical Company in Karamay, Xinjiang, completed a successful trial run on June 27, producing premium-grade rare-earth cis-butadiene rubber. The Chinese Academy of Sciences' Changchun Institute of Applied Chemistry announced the result on July 16.
The institute called the achievement a "major breakthrough" and said the core technologies are "fully under domestic control." It said the project would help meet "urgent demand for high-end grades ," support the petrochemical new-materials industry and help "safeguard supply-chain security."
The process makes two national-standard grades, BR1240 and BR1260, which differ in Mooney viscosity, a standard measure of rubber viscosity and processability. The rubber is made by polymerizing butadiene with a rare-earth catalyst, which helps control the polymer's molecular structure and, in turn, its mechanical properties.
Electric cars tend to be heavier than comparable gasoline vehicles and deliver high torque during acceleration, which places greater demands on tire durability. Low rolling resistance reduces the energy lost as tires deform and roll, while wear and fatigue resistance can extend tire life under repeated stress.
Heavy-duty vehicles also benefit from rubber that can withstand high loads, repeated deformation and heat build-up. Greater resistance to tearing and fatigue can improve durability under demanding conditions.
The institute says the rare-earth version beats conventional nickel-based butadiene rubber on wear resistance, strength, fatigue and tear resistance, low-temperature performance, heat build-up and rolling resistance .
The same properties could matter for military tires and other high-performance rubber parts, though the institute has disclosed nothing about supplying weapons or military vehicles.
The industrial result builds on more than six decades of work at the institute. In 1964, scientists Ouyang Jun and Shen Zhiquan published a paper on rare-earth compounds as catalysts for stereospecific polymerization. The institute describes it as the first international publication on using rare-earth catalysts to produce butadiene rubber.
Work on stereospecific polymerization catalyzed by rare-earth complexes won second prize in China's National Natural Science Award in 1982. Researchers including Bi Jifu, Jiang Liansheng and Zhang Xuequan later ran thousands of scale-up experiments and dozens of pilot trials to develop an industrial process.
A second-generation process led by Bi adds automation and domestically developed technology and equipment. His team tackled precise control of catalyst structure, catalyst preparation, tolerance of different feedstocks, and the integration of long-chain branching and functionalization.
The institute says its work progressed from meeting urgent needs of the national economy to supporting national defense modernization. Earlier defense-related work included liquid polysulfide rubber used as a binder for composite solid propellants, which supported China's "two bombs, one satellite" program.

Apple’s generative AI service, Apple Intelligence, has been registered for use on tablets and laptops in China, Shanghai’s cyberspace regulator announced on Monday. The move expands the service beyond smartphones and follows the company’s earlier regulatory approval for iPhones in July 2026.
China requires companies to register large language models and generative AI services with authorities before offering them to the public. The latest filing adds iPads and Mac laptops as approved uses for the service, clearing a key step toward broader availability across Apple’s device lineup in the mainland market.
Apple has developed a China-specific large language model with support from Alibaba, marking a shift from its approach in other markets. Alibaba’s Qwen model will provide text and image understanding and content generation capabilities through features such as Siri, writing tools, and visual intelligence. Alibaba has stated that these capabilities will be available to Chinese users across iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and visionOS.
The company has indicated that the features will arrive with the iOS 27.3 update in December 2026, following the release of a test version for developers on November 4. Earlier reporting has also noted involvement by Baidu in certain Apple Intelligence features for Chinese users.
The registration comes nearly two years after Apple Intelligence first launched in other markets, reflecting the time required to meet China’s regulatory standards for AI services. Expanding approval from iPhones to tablets and laptops is expected to support a more consistent AI experience across Apple’s ecosystem in China once the December rollout begins. ‎ MacDailyNews Take: Good news for Apple and for iPad and Mac sales in China, but as we wrote in November 2024 , “Apple Intelligence in China will be highly censored and rather limited; it will only spit back the approved narratives of the Chinese Communist Party.” The Chinese people are, unfortunately, acclimated to censorship and a lack of freedom, so iPad and Mac sales will increase with the advent of Apple Intelligence in China, regardless of the limitations placed upon it by the Chinese Communist Party.

articles.content_orig:
Everyone already knows about the code-in-a-box situation for GTA 6's physical edition on Xbox Series X|S and PS5, but we've also come to learn a few extra details in recent days about what to expect from the boxed copy of the game.
So, when you open up GTA 6 for Xbox Series X|S in physical form, you'll be presented with a code that will allow you to redeem the game on the Microsoft Store - essentially converting your physical purchase into a digital one.
Rockstar Games mentioned a shipping date of November 12th for the physical version a few days ago, but we've spotted some retailers saying they'll start shipping on the 11th instead, while a very small number of people even seem to have their copy already.
Once you've got the physical version in your hands, you'll be able to preload GTA 6 in full , although you can technically also do that from tonight by installing the game via the Xbox mobile app.
As you can also see from the tweet above, the physical edition is now confirmed to come with a double-sided A3 poster (at least if you buy from certain retailers). This poster appears to include the game's main artwork along with some character art on the back, so that's at least a nice little bonus to ease the pain of a disc-less release.
But what about a map? Well, Rockstar Games is handling the map a bit differently this time around, making a digital version available to download for free at launch. Alternatively, physical maps will be available to buy from the Rockstar Store "shortly after launch" for $0.99, but we reckon those will be in extreme demand and quickly sell out.
Of course, none of this really changes the fact that the physical edition of GTA 6 is kinda pointless for any platform as things stand, but it does at least make for a good display piece, and it'll be popular for gifting purposes this Christmas.
What's even weirder about this is that Rockstar is supporting GTA 6's launch with various other physical releases, such as an official soundtrack album and all kinds of merch , but it seems there's little hope for a disc version right now.

articles.title_orig: Trump talked with Fed chief, but there’s no record of it on Warsh’s calendar
articles.title_zh: Trump talked with Fed chief, but there’s no record of it on Warsh’s calendar
articles.content_orig:
Tom Boggioni is a writer, born, raised and living in San Diego — where he attended San Diego State University. Prior to writing for Raw Story, he wrote for FireDogLake, blogged as TBogg, and worked in banking, marketing and construction.
Democrats want answers from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh , demanding to know whether he is hiding secret conversations with Donald Trump .
The president says he and Warsh have talked. Warsh’s official records say they haven’t. And the Fed chair isn’t explaining the gap, the Washington Post reported.
On Friday, the Fed released Warsh’s September calendar, and once again, Trump’s name doesn’t appear. That makes "five months in a row," every month since Warsh took over in May, with no logged contact with the president. It comes despite a request this summer from Senate Democrats that he include any such conversations.
According to the Post, " The calendars are one of the few windows into how often a president reaches the official who leads the central bank’s decisions on interest rates , and previous Fed chairs have recorded interactions with presidents there. The Fed is designed to operate independently of the White House , setting rates based on its own best assessment of the economy rather than short-term political pressure."
On Sept. 16, the same day Warsh and his colleagues raised rates a quarter point against Trump’s wishes, the president told reporters he had weighed in on Warsh’s vote.
“I talked to Kevin, and I said, ‘You might as well vote with the board ’cause it’s not gonna matter,’” Trump said, noting that Warsh lacked the votes to change the outcome.
When a reporter asked if he had tried to sway Warsh, Trump said he hadn’t. “No, I didn’t convince him. No, I said, ‘Do what you want,’” he said, adding that he wanted Warsh “to be independent.”
Neither side has cleared it up, the report notes. The White House has refused to say when that conversation took place, and Warsh won’t confirm it ever happened.
Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-MD) and three other Democratic senators wrote to Warsh in August, asking him to state in writing whether he had spoken with Trump and to correct his calendars if so. Van Hollen’s office told the Post on Friday that Warsh never replied.
“It’s clear neither Warsh nor Trump give a damn about transparency to the American people,” Van Hollen said. “Under a Democratic majority in Congress, we will continue pushing for that much-needed transparency.”

Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman says CEO John Ternus is pressuring AI czar Craig Federighi to accelerate the Siri roadmap and deliver a powerful AI agent that can compete with OpenAI’s Dots or Meta’s Muse. While Federighi has delivered a functional version of Siri AI on an incredibly short timeline, the company has no illusions that it’s keeping pace with its rivals.
Two significant improvements are expected to be made to Siri in the coming months. One will give the assistant fine-grained control over Apple’s first-party apps, allowing it to do things like rotate and crop images in Photos and organize Safari tabs. Those capabilities are expected to land with iOS 27.3. The bigger change, integration with third-party apps, is likely to land later, in the Spring, according to Gurman. That would let Siri place an order through Grubhub or book a dinner reservation through OpenTable, for example.
But that’s just the start. Apple is expected to push Siri to become more agentic and enable features that will allow it to perform ongoing tasks, not just one-offs. Gurman says:
Dots, Muse and Grok can keep track of goals, determine what needs to happen next and continue pursuing objectives without the user initiating every individual step. Apple ultimately wants to go in this direction, I’m told, and I believe the company could make Siri more like an agent as early as next year — not that it has much of a choice, given current consumer and market demands.

[DAMASCUS] The Syrian Electricity Company signed an agreement with Chinese company Wasion Group Limited on Sunday to supply 6.5 million prepaid smart electricity meters, as part of efforts to modernize electricity consumption monitoring and improve power grid management in Syria. The deal raises questions about its cost, financing arrangements, and potential impact on consumers’ electricity bills.
The agreement was signed at the Syrian Electricity Company’s headquarters in Damascus, in the presence of representatives from both the Syrian and Chinese sides, as part of a broader government plan to modernize the energy sector and introduce digital systems into electricity services.
The media office of the Syrian Electricity Company, which operates under the Ministry of Energy, told The Media Line that the agreement includes the supply of 6 million single-phase meters, primarily intended for residential properties and small businesses, along with 500,000 three-phase meters, typically used by commercial and industrial facilities requiring greater electrical capacity.
According to the media office, the agreement also includes software systems and technical equipment necessary to operate the meters, allowing for more accurate consumption measurements, improved customer data management, reduced electricity losses, and more efficient network monitoring.
The media office explained that the prepaid metering system requires consumers to purchase electricity credit before using power, rather than paying periodic bills based on consumption recorded after use.
The new system is expected to improve electricity bill collection, reduce errors associated with traditional meter readings, and enable subscribers to monitor their electricity consumption more accurately.

It also did not clarify whether subscribers would be required to pay fees to replace their existing meters or how the prepaid system would be implemented for low-income households.
Authorities have also not announced a specific timetable for delivering all the meters covered by the agreement or identified which governorates will be included in the initial phase of implementation.
Khaled Abu Di, director of the General Establishment for Electricity Transmission and Distribution, previously announced that the institution had developed a plan to replace conventional electricity meters with smart meters over approximately three years.
In January 2026, Abu Di revealed that around 1.2 million electricity subscribers in Syria still lacked electricity meters, highlighting the scale of the challenges involved in modernizing metering, billing, and revenue collection systems.
The agreement comes as Syria’s electricity sector continues to face significant challenges following years of war, including damage to power generation facilities and transmission and distribution networks, as well as the need for substantial investment to rehabilitate infrastructure and improve the reliability of electricity supplies.
Although introducing smart meters could improve consumption management and reduce commercial electricity losses, modernizing metering systems does not necessarily mean an increase in electricity generation or an end to power outages. Improving the number of hours electricity is available also requires upgrading power plants, transmission and distribution networks, and securing reliable energy supplies.
The prepaid nature of the new meters raises additional questions about their impact on Syrian households, particularly amid difficult economic conditions and concerns about consumers’ ability to regularly purchase electricity credit.
It also remains unclear whether the government intends to introduce changes to electricity tariffs alongside the new system or will limit the initiative to modernizing metering and payment collection procedures.
The agreement represents another step in economic and technological cooperation between Syria and China, as Damascus seeks to attract foreign companies to participate in rehabilitating public services and infrastructure.

articles.title_orig: As War Roils Energy Markets, China Sees Its Emissions Drop
articles.title_zh: As War Roils Energy Markets, China Sees Its Emissions Drop
articles.content_orig:
Rooftop solar in Chengdu, China. Pexels
China’s carbon dioxide emissions have been flat or falling for more than two years as renewables stunt demand for fossil fuels. But the country just saw its steepest quarterly drop since the Covid pandemic, thanks to energy shocks rippling from the Iran war.
Between July and September, China saw its carbon dioxide emissions fall by 3.1 percent, according to an analysis of official figures and commercial data by Carbon Brief . That is the biggest quarterly decline since the 2022 pandemic lockdowns.
The analysis finds oil use fell by 4 percent, year on year, as Chinese drivers flocked to electric vehicles at a time when the Iran war is driving up the cost of fuel. Electric cars accounted for two in three new passenger vehicles sold in China in September, according to industry data . The uptake of electric cars has helped China ramp down oil imports in the wake of the conflict, analysts find .
Emissions from coal, meanwhile, fell by 3 percent, year on year, as the rapid growth of renewables far outstripped the rise in power demand. China added enough wind, solar, and nuclear generation over the same period to power Germany and more than twice as much as needed to meet China’s growing demand. Emissions from the production of steel and concrete also fell amid the ongoing construction slowdown.
China is continuing to build new coal plants despite the decline in coal generation. As the number of generators grows and the use of coal power declines, the average plant is seeing its running hours drop.
The shift from coal to renewables comes even as large volumes of solar and wind power go unused. China is now generating much more clean electricity than its power grid can handle. In the first six months of this year, China rejected roughly a quarter of its wind and solar output.
Analysts say that China lacks the transmission infrastructure necessary to ferry abundant clean energy from where it is generated to where it is needed. Also at issue is a policy that guarantees the purchase of electricity from newly built coal power plants.

articles.title_orig: EXCLUSIVE: Chinese Bag-Maker Songmont Enters Footwear
articles.title_zh: EXCLUSIVE: Chinese Bag-Maker Songmont Enters Footwear
articles.content_orig:
LONDON — Songmont, the Chinese brand that has made global headlines for cultural storytelling that resonates with China ‘s middle class, will launch its first footwear collection Wednesday.
Known for accessories that translate the landscapes, architecture and craft traditions of brand founder Fu Song’s hometown, Shanxi province, the brand is extending its offering beyond bags, ready-to-wear and fragrance with a footwear range inspired by the Wotou shoe.
Wotou is a traditional style named for its resemblance to a dome-shaped steamed corn bun popular in northern China . Traditionally handmade and padded with cotton, the model’s soft construction and distinctive raised seam informed Songmont’s contemporary interpretation for its debut footwear range.
The new silhouette launching this week, retailing for 2,680 renminbi, or $400, echoes the original, while piping joins two leather panels to recreate the ridge across the upper. Songmont’s tiger-tooth hardware adds a modern detail. The toe combines a square shape with softened edges, and layered leather forms a stepped heel inspired by Shanxi architecture. The style will come in 2.5cm and 6cm heel heights.
Songmont said it has spent more than a year developing the shoes, with 20-plus rounds of fittings and refinements. A custom last was designed to accommodate a range of foot shapes, and the use of full-grain cowhide uppers, a double-layer construction, sheepskin lining and high-resilience cotton insoles is meant to balance support, softness and breathability.
The brand added that the footwear launch builds on a design language it has developed across its collections. Its Gather bag, for example, recalls camel bags of the ancient Silk Road, while the Song bucket bag takes cues from traditional kite frameworks.
“As long as we choose things we genuinely like, the brand remains consistent. If we always chase trends or pay too much attention to what’s new, we can end up not knowing what we want,” Fu said about the brand’s approach in an earlier interview with WWD in Paris.
Founded in 2013, Songmont has around 20 stores in China and is expanding at a measured pace, with a focus on customer experience. It plans to open its first Hong Kong store in December, adding a new address as the brand continues to grow beyond mainland China.

articles.title_orig: KFC’s arrival at Italian ski slopes angers food and mountain purists
articles.title_zh: KFC’s arrival at Italian ski slopes angers food and mountain purists
articles.content_orig:
Fast-food outlets at two prestigious Dolomites resorts are Italy’s first, with legal action threatened
Europe live – latest updates
Skiers on the slopes of two of Italy’s most prestigious resorts will be able to dine from buckets of fried chicken between runs this winter as the US fast-food chain KFC prepares to open outlets, infuriating mountain and food purists while prompting a prominent businessman to threaten legal action.
KFC will open its first high-altitude restaurants on the slopes of Cortina d’Ampezzo and Madonna di Campiglio, in the Dolomites, on 5 December, an initiative the company said was aimed at “surprising people” and “reaching places” where nobody would expect to find it.
The move marks a debut for any fast-food outlet on an Italian ski slope, bringing a menu replete with KFC’s most popular products, from spicy wings and burgers to traditional buckets of fried chicken.
The plans appear to have taken people by surprise, not least Alberico Zardini, a majority shareholder in Faloria Spa, the company that manages the infrastructure on Mount Faloria in Cortina d’Ampezzo, where there is to be a KFC at 2,123 metres.
“The mere idea is disgraceful,” Zardini told Il Messaggero . “It’s absurd and shameful to imagine a fast-food joint in the most beautiful spot in Cortina. Do the people of Cortina not realise what we’re risking here?”
Zardini said he had written to the bosses of Faloria warning that he would pursue legal action unless they put the brakes on KFC’s mountain ambitions.
He said it was “a mad decision”, especially because the outlet would be selling fried chicken inside the Faloria mountain club, where a luxury lodge is due to open on an upper floor. “I am 100% against it and will not just sit back and watch,” he said.
The KFC in Madonna di Campiglio, in south-western Trentino on the opposite side of the Dolomites, will be at 1,700 metres on Piana di Nambino, next door to a swish après-ski club.
The two outlets came under the fast food chain’s “quick service restaurants” product range and were the company’s way of targeting a broader market beyond its loyal Gen Z customers, “from young families to mountain lovers”, said Marzia Farè, the chief marketing officer for KFC Italia.
“We strongly wanted this project because it perfectly represents the way we imagine the evolution of KFC: continuing to surprise, reaching places where no one would expect to find us, and doing so without giving up what makes us unique,” she told brandnews.it .
after newsletter promotion
Needless to say, with the cost of ski passes in Italy increasing each year, the outlets will appeal to those looking for cheap food in otherwise extremely pricey resorts.
But Oscar Farinetti, the founder of Eataly, Italy’s high-end food-store chain, has said the brand “doesn’t belong here at all” – while pointing the blame at customers. “We Italian consumers should be a tad more cultured,” he told Il Sole 24 Ore . “We need to acknowledge our assets – our cuisine made of few ingredients and excellent products. There is a lack of studying one’s own roots – we’re eating fried chicken instead of a nice slice of salami with a glass of fresh wine.”
Luigi Casanova from Mountain Wilderness, an NGO that works to protect mountain environments, told Corriere della Sera : “The era of polenta and luganega sausage is over,” while Paola Demagri, from Trentino’s provincial council, spoke about mountain identity being “sold out to Kentucky chicken”.
Others were more measured in their response. Cristian Ferrari, the president of Società Alpinisti Tridentini, the oldest mountain association in the Trentino area, said: “We have nothing against fried chicken, but are we sure this is the issue we should be most worried about?”

articles.title_orig: Birds return to waterfowl park after oil vandalism
articles.title_zh: Birds return to waterfowl park after oil vandalism
articles.content_orig:
Resident birds have returned to Broughshane Waterfowl Park after an oil spill which caused the death of 13 of the flock.
The popular attraction in County Antrim was forced to close after a nearby home heating oil tank was vandalised , causing the oil spill into the pond.
In a post on social media, The Waterfowl Pond confirmed that work is still underway to address the oil contamination and that a number of pens remain out of bounds.
More than 20 birds were transported to the USPCA's headquarters for urgent specialist care following the incident.
The park, which was home to 120 birds, has since reopened.
Broughshane Environment Wildfowl and Wildlife Trust's chairman, Gary Hayward, said about 10-12 birds have returned including two black swans and Nenes.
Hayward said they are back safely in their pens and they are lucky to be healthy.
The Northern Ireland Environment Agency (NIEA) was first alerted to the incident on Thursday 22 October and have been involved in removing the oil waste.
The agency said the substance involved had been identified as home heating oil or kerosene.
Police said about 44 gallons (200 litres) of oil had leaked from the tank which had been damaged at a business premise in the Main Street area of Broughshane.
Hayward said that there is very little evidence of the oil left as the NIEA have removed the majority of it.
"They have made problems a lot less than they could have been," he told BBC News NI.
He said there is still some oil around the edges, and once the oil leaves the pens the birds will be moved back into them.
The USPCA has also been a key part of the rescue operation.
They said that all of the birds, including geese, ducks and swans, needed bathed and treated due to the level of contamination they suffered.
Unfortunately some had already ingested too much and died as a result.
The Waterfowl Pond offered thanks to the USPCA for looking after the birds.
"We are truly grateful for everything you have done."
It also paid tribute to the support received from the public.
"It's another positive step forward for our park, and we couldn't have got here without you."
Police have said that enquiries into the incident are ongoing and have appealed to anyone with information to come forward.
